context.in_practice: There is only one route. Every command takes the same lock before it touches the config, including the read-only `history` command, because loading history may import changes. A `set` keeps the lock for its whole job: reading the file, reconciling it, writing it back and recording the change in history. A second command started meanwhile waits until the first is done, so two `set`s can't overwrite each other and every write has its history entry before anyone else looks. A running `watch` doesn't keep the lock for its whole run. It takes the lock only while it handles one detected change, then lets it go. So `watch` can run for hours without blocking other commands, which only wait for a moment if they arrive while `watch` is handling a change. Because the history entry is written before the lock is released, `watch` never sees a file change from a `set` before that change's history entry exists. Anyone maintaining the code has one rule to follow: anything that reads or changes the config or its history goes through the same lock.
context.stakes: Whether two commands run at the same moment, like a `set` while `watch` is running, can step on each other: one could overwrite the other's change to the config file, or the change history could lose an entry or show it out of order.
context.tradeoff: Route 1: every command, `history` included, may wait briefly for another command to finish, and a slow `set` makes the others wait for its full read, reconcile, write and record. In exchange, writes never collide and history always matches the file.

plan_why: This question is about which commands take an internal lock and how long they hold it. That only shows up when processes overlap, but the sandbox runs commands one at a time and forbids `watch` (concurrent writers are also out of contract). Sequential commands behave the same whatever the lock covers, so no example can make this route visible.
routes: Every command (history too) takes it; set holds it through load, reconcile, write and record; watch holds it only per reconcile
